subject: Accountancy
central_question: How does accounting identify, measure, record and communicate financial information so that different users can make informed decisions?
in_scope_units: Meaning of accounting and its development from record keeping into an information system.
Economic events and the stages of identification, measurement, recording and communication.
Organisations and internal and external users of accounting information.
Accounting as a source of information, its branches and qualitative characteristics.
Objectives and changing role of accounting.

Basic accounting terms including entity, transaction, assets, liabilities, capital, drawings, revenue, expenses, gains, profit, loss, purchases, sales, stock, debtors, creditors, vouchers and discounts.
banned_topics: Detailed accounting concepts and conventions, which belong to Theory Base of Accounting.
Journal entries, ledger posting and accounting equations, which belong to Recording of Transactions – I.
Preparation of trading, profit and loss account and balance sheet, which belongs to Financial Statements.

known_pitfalls.claim: Accounting and book-keeping are exactly the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Book-keeping mainly records transactions, while accounting also identifies, measures, summarises, analyses, interprets and communicates information.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every important event is recorded in financial accounts.
known_pitfalls.correction: Only events of financial character that can be measured in money are recorded.

known_pitfalls.claim: Only owners and managers use accounting information.
known_pitfalls.correction: External users such as investors, lenders, suppliers, government, customers and regulators also use it.

known_pitfalls.claim: Reliable information only means that the arithmetic is correct.
known_pitfalls.correction: Reliability also requires faithful representation, neutrality, freedom from bias and verifiability.

known_pitfalls.claim: Profit and cash balance are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Profit is excess of revenue over expenses for a period; cash is only one asset.
